Chapter 1: Ambition Begins with Wanting More Than What’s Given.
Think back to that moment—maybe early in your own career, or when you first started a creative project—when everything around you felt kind of... set in stone. The rules were clear, expectations were spelled out, and it almost felt like someone else had already mapped your path for you. It’s easy, in those moments, to look at others and think, “Well, they just have it. They’re the naturals.” But, you know, there’s something else bubbling just under the surface—something quieter, but way more powerful. It’s that simple, persistent hunger to reach for more—to do more, to be more—than what you were handed.
Picture this: you’re sitting at your desk, watching as other people get the best assignments, the loudest praise, the biggest chances. You might catch yourself thinking, “Maybe they really are better than me. Maybe I’m missing something.” But here’s the thing—over time, something becomes crystal clear. The folks who move ahead? They aren’t always the most talented in the room. They’re just the ones who want it the most—the ones who actually step up, who aren’t afraid to ask for more, or to risk looking silly if it means growing a little.
Especially in creative fields, this kind of hunger sometimes gets misread. Maybe a junior designer keeps tossing out ideas, even after hearing “not yet” or “that’s not the way we do things.” Colleagues might roll their eyes, but quietly, people notice that persistence. That drive to improve, to contribute, to be part of something bigger—it starts to change the energy of the whole place. It’s not about being the best right from the start. It’s about wanting to get better, and being willing to do what it takes to make that happen.
Real ambition isn’t loud or flashy. It’s that quiet choice to stay late and redo a project. To ask for honest feedback, even when it stings. To volunteer for the tasks nobody else wants. Over time, these small acts—these moments of wanting more—start to add up. The person who keeps reaching, keeps learning, keeps asking? They begin to stand out. Not because they’re born brilliant, but because they’re relentlessly curious and driven.
Most people really underestimate what it means to want something enough to go after it. They wait for a sign, or for someone to tell them they’re ready, or for permission to take the next step. But honestly? Just wanting more—setting your sights higher than what seems possible—creates its own momentum. It opens doors that would’ve stayed shut.
Whether it’s advertising, design, or any creative path you choose, here’s what often separates those who make it from those who don’t: the willingness to want more, to ask for more, and to believe you can always get better. The most successful people aren’t always the most gifted. They’re the ones who refuse to settle for what’s given—and who keep chasing what could be.
